{{One source|date=November 2013}}
In mathematics, the '''Bismut connection <math>\nabla</math>''' is the unique [[connection (mathematics)|connection]] on a complex [[Hermitian manifold]] that satisfies the following conditions,
# It preserves the metric <math>\nabla g =0</math> 
# It preserves the complex structure <math>\nabla J=0</math>
# The [[torsion (algebra)|torsion]] <math>T(X,Y)</math> contracted with the metric, i.e. <math>T(X,Y,Z)=g(T(X,Y),Z)</math>, is totally [[skew-symmetric matrix|skew-symmetric]]. 
[[Bismut]] has used this connection when proving a local index formula for the Dolbeault operator on non-[[Kähler manifold]]s. Bismut connection has applications in type II and heterotic string theory.

The explicit construction goes as follows. Let <math>\langle-,-\rangle</math> denote the pairing of two vectors using the metric that is Hermitian w.r.t the complex structure, i.e. <math>\langle X,JY\rangle=-\langle JX,Y\rangle</math>. Further let <math>\nabla</math> be the [[Levi-Civita connection]]. Define first a tensor <math>T</math> such that <math>T(Z,X,Y)=-\frac12\langle Z,J(\nabla_{X}J)Y\rangle </math>. This tensor is anti-symmetric in the first and last entry, i.e. the new connection <math>\nabla+T</math> still preserves the metric. In concrete terms, the new connection is given by <math>\Gamma^{\alpha}_{\beta\gamma}-\frac12 J^{\alpha}_{~\delta}\nabla_{\beta}J^{\delta}_{~\gamma}</math> with <math>\Gamma^{\alpha}_{\beta\gamma}</math> being the Levi-Civita connection. The new connection also preserves the complex structure. However, the tensor <math>T</math> is not yet totally anti-symmetric; the anti-symmetrization will lead to the [[Nijenhuis tensor]]. Denote the anti-symmetrization as <math>T(Z,X,Y)+\textrm{cyc~in~}X,Y,Z=T(Z,X,Y)+S(Z,X,Y)</math>, with <math>S</math> given explicitly as

:<math>S(Z,X,Y)=-\frac12\langle X,J(\nabla_{Y}J)Z\rangle-\frac12\langle Y,J(\nabla_{Z}J)X\rangle.</math> 
<math>S</math> still preserves the complex structure, i.e. <math>S(Z,X,JY)=-S(JZ,X,Y)</math>.

:<math>\begin{align} 
S(Z,X,JY)+S(JZ,X,Y)&=-\frac12\langle JX, \big(-(\nabla_{JY}J)Z-(J\nabla_ZJ)Y+(J\nabla_YJ)Z+(\nabla_{JZ}J)Y\big)\rangle\\
&=-\frac12\langle JX, Re\big((1-iJ)[(1+iJ)Y,(1+iJ)Z]\big)\rangle.\end{align}</math>
So if <math>J</math> is integrable, then above term vanishes, and the connection

:<math>\Gamma^{\alpha}_{\beta\gamma}+T^{\alpha}_{~\beta\gamma}+S^{\alpha}_{~\beta\gamma}.</math>
gives the Bismut connection.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://iris.uniroma1.it/retrieve/15f8f116-9574-4a91-a6eb-6751ebf37a11/Tesi_dottorato_Barbaro.pdf|title=The Geometry of the Bismut Connection|last=Barbaro|first=Giuseppe|accessdate=1 November 2024}}</ref>
